name: Merrowby
unique_feature: built around the bell's crater; the Toll's lip is a tavern cellar

name: Tamwick
unique_feature: the only cider press

name: Wardens' Rest

name: Hollin Barrow
unique_feature: the Barrow Reeve's bell-hammer
formed_by: a collapsed crypt cut into chalk, then a yew's roots

name: Pennywort's Mill
unique_feature: a wheel that turns with no water

name: The Chalk Hound
unique_feature: a hill figure whose eye you can lie in

name: The Cracked Toll
unique_feature: a forty-metre bronze bell half-buried in a hillside

name: Tollmere
unique_feature: canals, charter-boards, and a hinge-less Oroth door that opens for names

name: Gullhithe
unique_feature: drying racks of lake-eel and the Lamp keeper's cottage

name: The Lamp
unique_feature: a lighthouse whose light is an Oroth sul-stone

name: The Sayers' Spire
unique_feature: a black Oroth stalk with a brass crown of human construction

name: The Undercroft
unique_feature: the Quiet Hands' hall inside a bell
formed_by: Oroth foundations, then sewers cut by the guilds

name: The Sunken Barge
unique_feature: the lake serpent's nest
formed_by: a guild barge that sank with its cargo

name: Isseva
unique_feature: the water-burial jetty

name: Nauve's Landing
unique_feature: the boatwright's upturned-hull hall

name: The Drowned Nave

formed_by: an Oroth Harmony that sank into the marsh

name: Eelfathom Pool
unique_feature: a pool whose reflection runs a few seconds behind

name: Grandfather Hollow
unique_feature: a town inside a dead tree ninety metres tall

name: The Grandfather
unique_feature: lights in the knots of a hollow giant

name: Fernhold
unique_feature: the antler hall

name: The Standing Moot
unique_feature: a stone circle that hums when you stand in its centre

name: Weaverdeep
unique_feature: silk bridges over root chasms
formed_by: root caverns under the Grandfather, widened by weavers

name: The Thornmarch
unique_feature: the living Briar wall

name: Kharrow Hold
unique_feature: a clan hold carved into a cliff, reached by a chain bridge

name: Brindlecrag
unique_feature: mine headframes and bone lintels

name: The Fallen Hand
unique_feature: a giant's stone hand with a shrine in its palm

name: Oskeld Mine
unique_feature: the singing shaft
formed_by: a clan mine following a silver vein into giant bone

name: Frostmother's Cradle
unique_feature: ice that holds the shapes of what froze in it

name: Windgate Pass
unique_feature: the clan toll-house in the snow

name: Pilgrim's Ash
unique_feature: a chapter-house inside a fallen bell

name: Greyfold
unique_feature: tables still laid for a meal nobody finished

name: The Sunken Choir
unique_feature: twelve headless colossi in a ring

name: The Cantor's Seat
unique_feature: the note-light, a cold blue that has burned for a thousand years
formed_by: the Oroth Harmony that still holds its note

name: The Hushline
unique_feature: mist where colour and sound drain away

name: Ashwell
unique_feature: a well-house over the Lark Pool's outflow, its door-post notched every Naming Day with how far the grey has come up the glass bed
story: The first living village north of the ash. Carters water their horses here after the grey road, and nobody in Ashwell says the word south if they can say down instead.
hook: The notch on the well-house post is above last year's for the first time in a century, and the well-warden wants someone to walk the glass bed to the Choir and say why.

name: Wynstead
unique_feature: water-meadows flooded on purpose every spring through a chain of oak sluices
story: The Vale's hay comes off Wynstead's drowned meadows. The Wynsteads have kept the sluices since the Tending, and the Steward in Merrowby is the one of them who left.
hook: Someone has been opening the sluices at night, and the flood is drowning the lane where Gosford's name used to be; the sluice-keeper thinks that is the point.

name: Cressbourne
unique_feature: watercress beds stepped down the coombe in chalk-walled pools, each pool a family's
story: Cressbourne sells cress to Tollmere by the cartload and keeps the recipe for the green sauce the city thinks it invented.
hook: The top bed came up grey overnight, and the Cresswells want to know whether it is the water, the chalk or the Toll before the city tastes it.

name: Fallowfold
unique_feature: a dew pond lined with puddled chalk that has never once been dry, inside a fold of flint walls
story: The shepherds of the West Downs bring the flocks in off the grey border to Fallowfold's pond every evening, and wash the ash out of the fleeces there when the wind has been south.
hook: A ewe came back from the south pasture grey to the skin and will not go into the pond; the shepherd wants her named, and does not know by whom.

name: Bramcombe
unique_feature: a sheep-wash in the combe bottom fed by a spring piped through a hollowed oak trunk
story: The downs' flocks are washed and counted at Bramcombe before shearing; a tally-stick hangs in the doorway of every house, and every one of them is one notch short.
hook: Every tally in the combe is one sheep short every morning, and no sheep is missing.

name: Rookdown
unique_feature: a rookery of a thousand nests in the elms over the green, and not one rook will fly south of it
story: The last village on the Brow before the cliff and the Hush. There is a grey patch on the green the size of a threshing floor, and every year it is a little bigger.
hook: The grey patch on the green has reached the well: half the village wants to leave and half says leaving is how a village goes quiet, and they want somebody from outside to say which half is right.

name: Hazelcombe
unique_feature: hurdle-makers' yards stacked to the eaves with woven hazel panels, and every fold in the Vale came out of them
story: Hazelcombe weaves the hurdles every sheepfold in Hearthvale is made of, from rods the Woodfolk cut at the wood's edge and sell them at a price both sides find insulting.
hook: The Wardens have ordered a mile of hurdles for new pens on the grey border, and the weavers want to know what the pens are for before they weave them.

name: The Hare and Hurdle
unique_feature: a coaching inn at the downs' crossroads whose sign, a hare leaping a hurdle, is repainted every Long Table by whoever lost at skittles
story: Drovers, carters bound for the Brow and Wardens off the border all drink at the Hare and Hurdle, the only roof between Tamwick and Rookdown.
hook: The innkeeper's board of who owes whom a drink has one debt on it, in chalk that will not rub off, owed to a man nobody can remember.

name: The Last Camp
unique_feature: a camp on the rim above the Hush for the ones who have decided, where nobody asks anyone anything
story: Pilgrims who have made up their minds wait here a night, a month or three years before they walk to the Stair. The Order brings bread and does not stay to talk, because the Vigil Book says not to make a fuss.
hook: A pilgrim who has waited three years asks for the one thing she has not been able to find out: whether anybody would say her name if she stayed.

name: The West Walk
unique_feature: an Order watch-post walled with the doors of Ashcombe's houses, facing the grey marsh
story: The knights of the west walk sleep here between rounds. It was Ossel's forge until the autumn of 1019; the Order still quenches in her trough and nobody has lit her forge since.
hook: Someone has been working Ossel's forge at night, and what they are making is a bell-bearer's clapper.

name: Stride's Foot
unique_feature: the Tallymen's toll-house and weighbridge at the south end of the Long Stride, under a row of limes
story: Everything that goes to Tollmere on wheels is weighed here and priced. The toll-clerks keep the busiest ledger in Wickmere, and the inn beside them keeps the second.
hook: One traveller a week is entered in the toll-ledger going out to the city and never coming back, always in the same hand, and the hand is not a clerk's.

name: Sedgehithe
unique_feature: a reed-cutters' landing where the punts are tied to a row of Oroth bollards shaped like bells
story: The Mere's western reed fringe is cut from Sedgehithe for Tollmere's thatch and the Sayers' lamp-wicks. The cutters are half Lakefolk and half reedfolk and sing both kinds of song, badly.
hook: The reed fringe is dying back from the shore in a straight line, as if something were drawing a rule across the water.

name: Merrowhithe
unique_feature: pike smokehouses hung in the arches of a broken Oroth aqueduct that brings no water
story: The quietest shore of the Mere. Merrowhithe smokes pike for Tollmere and has no opinion about anything, which the city finds restful and the Sayers find suspicious.
hook: The dry aqueduct has started to drip, and there is nothing upstream of it but Skerrow.

name: Moreva
unique_feature: an eel-landing whose stilt-houses are strung with wicker eel-traps like washing
story: Moreva traps the North Channel from the Heron Watch to the Nave and sells to Isseva, Gullhithe and anyone else who can stand the smell on the boards.
hook: The eel-traps have started coming up full of something that is not eels, with a lantern-maker's knot tied round it.

name: Saeva
unique_feature: the lantern-makers' landing, where burial lanterns are woven from rush dyed in marsh indigo and hung in their hundreds to dry
story: Every lantern that goes out on the water at Isseva was made at Saeva, and every lantern-maker there can tell you whose it was by the weave.
hook: A lantern came back up the channel against the current, in a weave the lantern-makers stopped using eighty years ago.

name: Nauvissa
unique_feature: a reed-bed hamlet on the grey edge where the reeds come up ash-coloured and are sold to the Tolling Order for candle-wicks
story: Nauvissa cuts the reeds nobody else will, the grey ones, and the Order buys every bundle. The reedfolk say grey reed burns with a flame you can hear.
hook: The grey moves up the Greyreed a reed-bed a year; Nauvissa wants to know which of the four accounts is right before they decide whether to move.

name: Oulea
unique_feature: salt pans cut into the tideflats and a salt-boilers' hamlet on a shell bank above the highest tide
story: The only salt in Wickmere not bought from the Salt Isles. Oulea boils brine over driftwood and sells it to Isseva, who sell it to the city as Salt Isles salt, and everybody knows.
hook: The tide came in over the shell bank for the first time in anyone's memory, and left something on the pans.

name: Elderhold
unique_feature: a woodfolk lodge built inside a ring of elder trees whose doorposts are still growing
story: Elderhold is the Wold's door on the Mere side. The rafters' logs are chosen here, and a stranger who wants to go further in asks here, and is usually told no, politely, in the Wold's way.
hook: The elder doorposts have flowered out of season, and the lodge wants the Standing Moot's opinion without going to ask for it.

name: Rookhold
unique_feature: the gate-keepers' lodge, its roof thatched with cut Briar and its door with no latch on the inside
story: Rookhold keeps the Old Gate, the only one of the Briar's four whose doors still close. The keepers take turns sleeping against the gate, and the one on duty is always the youngest.
hook: The Old Gate's doors were found open at dawn, from the far side.

name: Hazelwick
unique_feature: a coppicers' hamlet among hazel stools so old they are wider than the cottages
story: Hazelwick has cut the same hazel on a seven-year round since before Tollmere had a charter. Every stool has a name and a family, and the families are not always on speaking terms.
hook: One of the stools has not grown back after cutting, the first in seven hundred years, and the family it belongs to wants it named before the Roll takes theirs.

name: Ormhold
unique_feature: a lodge of black-ash timbers under the Northwold's oldest oak, where the Circle's Listeners slept before the northern gate
story: Ormhold is as far north as the Woodfolk live. The Circle's Listeners slept here in 1038 on their way through the northern gate, and the lodge still charges the Circle for the beds.
hook: The Listeners left a trunk at Ormhold in 1038 and never came back for it; it has started to smell of the sea.

name: Ruddow
unique_feature: Clan Rudd's hold of turf-roofed longhouses behind a wall of giant's vertebrae
story: Rudd are herders and the Moot's oldest creditors: Kharrow owes them forty head and a hearth for the winter of the long snow, and Rudd will not take payment, which is how one clan keeps another in its debt.
hook: Rudd have finally asked for the forty head, through the player as Kharrow's go-between, and the reason is on the roll of their dead.

name: Ghastfell
unique_feature: Clan Ghast's hold across a gorge whose chain bridge was broken in the year of the broken bridge, reached ever since by ladders
story: The Moot forgave Ghast its blood-debt, and the forgiveness is sung every morning so that it stays forgiven. Ghast has never mended its bridge, which the other clans take as a remark.
hook: Ghast want the bridge mended and the song of forgiveness stopped; Kharrow want neither.

name: Dreughow
unique_feature: Clan Dreugh's hold cut into a limestone scar, its doors painted with the first verse of the Rope-Song
story: Dreugh sing first at the Moot, and paint the first verse on their doors so a stranger knows the order of things before he knocks.
hook: Someone has painted an eighth verse on a Dreughow door overnight, in no clan's hand.

name: Skarlow
unique_feature: Clan Skarl's hold of beehive huts on a limestone pavement, every hut's door facing east
story: The easternmost clan, herders of the Skarl Fells, who face east because their verse says the giants went that way and will come back by it.
hook: Skarl's herders have seen a line of lights moving north along the Briar, beyond the wall, where there is no road.

name: Oskelcrag
unique_feature: Clan Oskel's mining village of stone rows built on the spoil heaps of the old Oskeld workings
story: Oskel dug the Oskeld mine until the singing started, and sealed it, and now dig lead in the lower dale and do not talk about silver. They walk past the mine road without looking up it.
hook: An Oskel child walked up the mine road in her sleep and came back humming.
